name: HUB Bootloader
description: UDS flash sequence for this ECU's bootloader.

security._comment: All four security levels share one algorithm - four doors to one room, not graded access. This ECU also requires SecurityAccess before entering the Programming session, unlike the standard SLP3 order - see before_programming.

sequence._comment_dtc_comm: APP now implements both (see APP/Src/UDS_CFG/UDS_config.c): ControlDTCSetting ($85) gates FAULT_MGR's DTC storage, CommunicationControl ($28) gates MSG_SCHED's non-diagnostic CAN TX (sensor telemetry + heartbeat). Defaults for comm_ctrl_subtype_disable/comm_ctrl_type (0x03/0x03) match what APP's handler accepts.
sequence._comment_preconditions: APP now implements CheckProgrammingPreconditions (RoutineControl $0203, see uds_handle_check_programming_preconditions() in APP/Src/UDS_CFG/UDS_config.c) - infrastructure only, always reports every precondition fulfilled since this product has no real interlock defined yet.
sequence._comment_erase: Erase honours an optional address/size option record, sector-aligning and bounds-checking it, so each datablock only erases its own region instead of the whole area every time. Omitting the option record (routine_erase_send_addr_size=false) erases the whole configured region instead.
sequence._comment_fingerprint: FBL now implements 0x2E WriteDataByIdentifier for the fingerprint DID (see fbl_uds_handle_write_fingerprint() in FBL/Src/UDS_CFG/UDS_config.c), persisted via FBL's own dedicated NVM page. did_fingerprint is set explicitly to 0xF184 (applicationSoftwareFingerprint, ISO 14229-1 Table C.1) since that's what FBL actually implements - this tool's own default (0xF15A) does not match and would NRC requestOutOfRange if left unset.
sequence._comment_checksum: This ECU has no per-segment checksum routine, only a whole-region one - see routine_validate_all.
sequence._comment_validate: FBL now accepts an optional 4-byte big-endian expected-CRC32 in the routine's Option Record: send it and FBL reports back a single pass($00)/fail($01) status byte instead of a raw CRC (see FBL_uds_handle_check_memory() in xCOMMON_MODULES/Src/FBL/FBL.c). Sending no Option Record keeps the old raw-CRC response for backward compatibility. This tool still only checks that the request itself didn't NRC - it does not yet send the expected CRC or check the status byte, so a bad transfer still isn't caught until BM's post-reset validation. Wiring that up is a CANFLASH-side follow-up, not an FBL firmware change.
